summary: High-level technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, joint reference architecture, and next steps for a co-listed solution. Agreed on templated reference arch, compatibility tests, and contents required for marketplace submission. Identified a few open network/KMS questions and a follow-up compatibility test window.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off - Jordan from Redwood here, with Priya our solutions eng. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Carlos Mendez: Carlos here, head of partnerships at LuminaCloud. Amina, Ravi and Leah on.
[00:15] Priya Natarajan: Hi all, Priya. Nervous about screen share but I can - I can share the arch in a bit.
[00:22] Amina Saleh: Amina, solutions architect. Good to meet you.
[00:27] Jordan Ellis: Awesome. Agenda: marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture, joint packaging and commercial touch points, then action items. Any other items?
[00:36] Ravi Patel: Quick question on billing flow, if that's okay to slot in?
[00:40] Jordan Ellis: Yes, we'll do billing during the commercial piece.
[00:44] Priya Natarajan: I'll start with the reference arch. Share screen?
[00:48] (screen share starts)
[01:02] Priya Natarajan: So here's a high level - sorry, little lag - Redwood runtime sits as the inference endpoint, either hosted by Redwood or deployed in the customers VPC for private deployments. We usually show three modes: hosted API, dedicated capacity and private deploy. You might see the term "Redwood dedicate" in older docs, that is a transcribe error sometimes.
[01:23] Leah Chen: For LuminaCloud listing we want to emphasize private option because many of our customers are regulated.
[01:28] Priya Natarajan: Yep, makes sense. In the ref arch we call out network flow: app -> LuminaCloud platform -> Redwood endpoint. If private, Redwood control plane is still redwood-managed, but data plane can be customer-managed in VPC or on-prem, KMS integration optional.
[01:46] Amina Saleh: Quick nit: for KMS, can customers bring their own HSM? We need that for our finance customers.
[01:51] Priya Natarajan: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; the current flow uses envelope encryption, you can see the key rotation note here. Sometimes the transcript will say "KMS H M M" which is a oops in the transcription.
[02:05] Carlos Mendez: Are there any hard latency SLOs when running private? Our customers often ask about 99th percentile numbers.
[02:12] Priya Natarajan: Good question. For hosted we quote typical p99 of ~250-350ms for mid-size models, but dedicated or private numbers vary based on instance type and seq length. We'll capture recommended instance types in the doc. Priya: I'll put a table in the draft.
[02:28] Jordan Ellis: Also for marketplace listing the thumbnail and screenshots matter, and we need a short blurb + bullets, product categories, tags. We have a template.
[02:36] Leah Chen: On commercial flow, we prefer marketplace bill-through with revenue share, but also need direct-contract options.
[02:42] Jordan Ellis: Yep, we can support both. For marketplace bill-through we need the billing contact and the connector details - sometimes Marketplace uses a billing API that requires account ID.
[02:53] Ravi Patel: For security docs, do you have SOC 2/ISO artifacts we can attach to the listing?
[02:58] Jordan Ellis: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts, plus SAML and RBAC docs. We'll share the security bundle link after.
[03:07] Amina Saleh: On the reference arch, what about fallbacks - like if dedicated capacity is full, what's the graceful degradation?
[03:12] Priya Natarajan: We implement smart routing & automatic fallback to compatible model variants; e.g., route to a quantized variant or fallback region. We'll call that out on the diagram.
[03:24] (brief cross talk)
[03:30] Jordan Ellis: Let's walk through marketplace checklist. Priya, can you open the template?
[03:34] Priya Natarajan: Yep - template includes: title, tagline, 200-word description, 3-5 screenshots, architecture diagram, supported regions, compliance notes, pricing options, support SLAs, contact info, and billing connector info.
[03:51] Carlos Mendez: For screenshots do you want live UI or mockups?
[03:55] Priya Natarajan: Mockups are fine; we usually prefer annotated diagrams too.
[03:59] Leah Chen: One concern: onboarding flow - we need a one-click deploy for the marketplace with default values, but also advanced mode for VPC. Is that supported?
[04:08] Priya Natarajan: Yes, our marketplace packaging supports both: a quickstart template that provisions a hosted listing and a VPC-connector template for private deploys. Some small differences on credentials.
[04:19] Ravi Patel: Network: we'll likely need specific outbound IPs for allowlisting. Can you provide static egress IP ranges for private deploys?
[04:26] Priya Natarajan: For private we don't usually require egress allowlisting unless customers want to lock down control-plane calls. We can provide IP ranges for managed egress; for fully private air-gapped, there's an on-prem package. We'll add the exact CIDR ranges to the doc.
[04:41] Jordan Ellis: On the reference arch diagram, action item: we'll annotate where KMS sits, where telemetry is sent, and the log retention options.
[04:50] Amina Saleh: About telemetry, can telemetry be routed to LuminaCloud's SIEM? We prefer to ingest logs into our Splunk.
[04:58] Priya Natarajan: Yes, we can ship audit logs to customer S3 or push to syslog/SIEM connectors; we just redact tokens by default. We'll add that as an integration pattern.
[05:12] (screen pause)
[05:18] Jordan Ellis: Commercial knobs: pricing tiers, reserved capacity for Dedicated, and a test credit for first 30 days. We'll include suggested wording.
[05:27] Carlos Mendez: Great. For joint go-to-market, what's the recommended co-branding guidelines?
[05:33] Jordan Ellis: We'll share a brand kit and guidelines in the partner portal; nothing strict but suggested lockups and logo usage.
[05:40] Priya Natarajan: Quick note: there's a compatibility caveat with some older quantized models when you enable KV cache, we should test on your typical prompts. That's one of the compatibility tests we proposed.
[05:54] Amina Saleh: OK can we schedule a test window where Redwood runs baseline perf vs our workload?
[05:59] Priya Natarajan: Yes - Priya to run compatibility test matrix. We'll need sample prompts and typical seq lengths from Lumina.
[06:08] Leah Chen: We'll share a sample prompt set and a couple of representative JSON payloads.
[06:13] Jordan Ellis: Perfect. On the listing timeline, we usually take 2 weeks to approve assets once submitted. Can we target a mid-April listing?
[06:21] Carlos Mendez: Mid-April sounds feasible, pending approvals.
[06:25] (background noise, inaudible for a few seconds)
[06:34] Priya Natarajan: Another small item: for private deploys using customer KMS we need the key policy details; could Amina share an example?
[06:42] Amina Saleh: Yes I'll pull a sample key policy.
[06:45] Jordan Ellis: Ok let's go through open risks quickly.
[06:49] Priya Natarajan: Risk 1: model compatibility with our runtime's quantized kernels - mitigated by compatibility tests.
[06:55] Jordan Ellis: Risk 2: network design for private customers who require strict egress - mitigated by on-prem package or explicit egress CIDRs.
[07:03] Amina Saleh: Risk 3: billing connector mismatch - we need to validate account IDs and test billing flow in sandbox.
[07:09] Jordan Ellis: We'll coordinate with finance once we have the billing contact.
[07:12] (crosstalk)
[07:20] Rachel (off): Sorry late to the call, joining now.
[07:25] Jordan Ellis: No problem. Back to the action items recap.
[07:28] Priya Natarajan: I'll run the test matrix and share results by April 9th. Need sample prompts and model sizes.
[07:36] Jordan Ellis: I'll draft the marketplace listing copy and attach screenshots, target 2026-04-02.
[07:42] Amina Saleh: I'll provide the deployment playbook and key policy by 2026-04-05.
[07:48] Carlos Mendez: I'll confirm billing contact and put the marketplace timeline on our side (due 2026-04-07).
[07:55] Leah Chen: Schedule follow-up next week to review the initial draft?
[07:59] Jordan Ellis: Let's tentatively schedule 2026-04-06 for a 30-minute review. I'll send calendar invite.
[08:06] (screen share ends)
[08:10] Jordan Ellis: Anything else?
[08:13] Ravi Patel: One last: who should we ping for SOC evidence?
[08:17] Jordan Ellis: Ping me and I'll route to security; we have an S3 link with the redacted bundle.
[08:22] Amina Saleh: Thanks everyone.
[08:25] Jordan Ellis: Thanks, we'll follow up with the doc links and invite. Bye.
[48:00] (meeting ended)
